result.summary: Conditionally logs Tor control port connection failures depending on whether Tor was explicitly configured. If -torcontrol, -torpassword, or -listenonion is set, failed connection attempts continue to log warnings; otherwise, the first failure is logged once at info level and subsequent retries are demoted to debug logging. It also adds an info log when an established Tor onion service is unexpectedly lost.
result.problem: Since commit eae193e750 in v32, failed Tor control port connections and periodic reconnect attempts log warnings unconditionally. On default-configured nodes without Tor running, this pollutes debug.log with roughly 18 warning lines every hour. Additionally, unexpectedly losing an active onion service connection lacked an info-level log.
evidence: PR description notes that since commit eae193e750 (in v32), on a default configured node without Tor, failed reconnect attempts pollute debug.log with 18 lines every hour.
Referenced issue #36691 highlights user friction where connections to the Tor control port could not be cleanly silenced or disabled.
result.changed_since_previous: Rather than unconditionally demoting all Tor connection failures to debug, the PR now keeps warnings if Tor options (-torcontrol, -torpassword, or -listenonion) are explicitly set. Unconfigured nodes now log an initial failure at info level before demoting retries to debug, and an info log was added for when an active onion service disconnects.
result.card: This PR refines Tor control port logging so that connection failure warnings are only emitted if Tor was explicitly configured via -torcontrol, -torpassword, or -listenonion. On default configurations without a local Tor daemon, the first failure is logged once at info level and subsequent retries are suppressed to the tor debug category, eliminating roughly 18 lines of warning noise per hour introduced in v32. It also adds an info-level log when an active onion service is unexpectedly lost.

risk.why: Mistakes are confined to Tor control daemon logging and would at most result in misleading or missing log lines.
